## 8.1 Project Structure for Healthcare GIS in Julia

A well-organized Julia project for healthcare GIS analysis should separate concerns into distinct layers: data acquisition, data processing and cleaning, spatial analysis, statistical modeling, and visualization. The following project structure is recommended as a starting template.

healthcare_geo/

├── Project.toml          # Package dependencies

├── Manifest.toml         # Exact dependency versions (auto-generated)

├── README.md             # Project documentation

├── src/

│   ├── HealthcareGeo.jl  # Main module file

│   ├── data/

│   │   ├── download.jl   # Data acquisition functions

│   │   ├── clean.jl      # Data cleaning/transformation

│   │   └── classify.jl   # Rural classification logic

│   ├── analysis/

│   │   ├── morans.jl     # Spatial autocorrelation

│   │   ├── accessibility.jl  # 2SFCA and variations

│   │   ├── gwr.jl        # Geographically weighted regression

│   │   └── clusters.jl   # LISA cluster analysis

│   └── viz/

│       ├── choropleth.jl # Choropleth mapping

│       ├── accessibility_map.jl

│       └── dashboard.jl  # Interactive dashboard

├── data/

│   ├── raw/              # Downloaded, unmodified source data

│   ├── processed/        # Cleaned, joined datasets

│   └── outputs/          # Analysis results, maps

├── notebooks/            # Pluto/Jupyter notebooks for exploration

└── test/

└── runtests.jl       # Unit and integration tests


## 8.2 Complete Spatial Analysis Pipeline

The following code implements a complete end-to-end spatial analysis pipeline for studying primary care access in rural counties. It demonstrates data loading, spatial join, accessibility calculation, Moran's I analysis, and choropleth map generation.

```julia
# === HealthcareGeo.jl: Main Module ===
module HealthcareGeo

using DataFrames, CSV, Statistics, LinearAlgebra
using Shapefile, ArchGDAL, GeoDataFrames, GeoInterface
using GeoMakie, CairoMakie
using HTTP, JSON

export load_counties, load_providers, build_weights_matrix,
       compute_morans_i, two_step_fca, lisa_clusters,
       make_choropleth_map

include("data/download.jl")
include("data/classify.jl")
include("analysis/morans.jl")
include("analysis/accessibility.jl")
include("viz/choropleth.jl")

end  # module
# === analysis/accessibility.jl ===

"""
```

Build a spatial weights matrix from county geometries.

Uses queen contiguity: two polygons are neighbors if they share any boundary.

Returns a row-standardized matrix.

"""

```julia
function build_queen_weights(geoms::Vector)::Matrix{Float64}
    n = length(geoms)
    W = zeros(Float64, n, n)
    for i in 1:n
        for j in (i+1):n
            if GeoInterface.intersects(geoms[i], geoms[j])
                W[i,j] = 1.0
                W[j,i] = 1.0
            end
        end
    end
    # Row-standardize
    row_sums = sum(W; dims=2)
    for i in 1:n
        if row_sums[i] > 0
            W[i,:] ./= row_sums[i]
        end
    end
    return W
end

"""
Compute LISA cluster categories for each spatial unit.
Returns Vector{String} with values: "HH", "LL", "HL", "LH", "NS"
"""
function lisa_clusters(values::Vector{Float64}, W::Matrix{Float64};
                        permutations::Int = 999,
                        significance::Float64 = 0.05)::Vector{String}
    n = length(values)
    x_bar = mean(values)
    z = values .- x_bar
    s2 = sum(z.^2) / n

    # Local Moran's I for each location
    Wz = W * z
    I_local = (z ./ s2) .* Wz

    # Permutation test for each location
    p_values = ones(Float64, n)
    for i in 1:n
        perm_I = Vector{Float64}(undef, permutations)
        perm_z = copy(z)
        for k in 1:permutations
            shuffle!(perm_z)
            perm_I[k] = (z[i] / s2) * dot(W[i,:], perm_z)
        end
        p_values[i] = mean(abs.(perm_I) .>= abs(I_local[i]))
    end

    # Classify: only report significant clusters
    result = fill("NS", n)
    for i in 1:n
        if p_values[i] < significance
            hi_val = values[i] >= x_bar
            # Spatial lag sign
            lag_hi = dot(W[i,:], values) >= x_bar
            result[i] = if hi_val && lag_hi; "HH"
                         elseif !hi_val && !lag_hi; "LL"
                         elseif hi_val && !lag_hi; "HL"
                         else "LH" end
        end
    end
    return result
end
```


## 8.3 Integrating OpenStreetMap for Network Analysis

Accurate travel time analysis requires road network data. OpenStreetMapX.jl provides Julia-native functionality for working with OpenStreetMap (OSM) data, including parsing PBF/OSM files, building routing graphs, and computing shortest paths. For large-scale analysis, the OSRM HTTP API provides fast routing calculations that can be batched for accessibility analysis at scale.

```julia
using OpenStreetMapX, HTTP, JSON

"""
Batch travel time calculation via OSRM public API.
origins:      Vector of (lat, lon) tuples for population centroids
destinations: Vector of (lat, lon) tuples for provider locations
```

Returns Matrix{Float64} of travel times in minutes (n_origins × n_dest)

"""

```julia
function osrm_travel_times(origins::Vector{NTuple{2,Float64}},
                            destinations::Vector{NTuple{2,Float64}})::Matrix{Float64}
    # OSRM table service: computes all-pairs travel times
    # Note: public API has rate limits; use self-hosted OSRM for production
    base_url = "http://router.project-osrm.org/table/v1/driving/"

    # Build coordinate string: lon,lat;lon,lat;...
    all_coords = vcat(origins, destinations)
    coord_str = join(["$(lon),$(lat)" for (lat,lon) in all_coords], ";")
    src_str = join(0:(length(origins)-1), ";")
    dst_str = join(length(origins):(length(all_coords)-1), ";")

    url = base_url * coord_str * "?sources=$(src_str)&destinations=$(dst_str)"
    resp = HTTP.get(url)
    data = JSON.parse(String(resp.body))

    # Convert seconds to minutes, replace nothing with Inf
    times = data["durations"]
    n_orig = length(origins)
    n_dest = length(destinations)
    result = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n_orig, n_dest)
    for i in 1:n_orig, j in 1:n_dest
        t = times[i][j]
        result[i,j] = isnothing(t) ? Inf : t / 60.0
    end
    return result
end
```
